newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam smashes illegal coal mines, arrests owners.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam smashes illegal coal mines, arrests owners.

text.p: Authorities in Vietnam's northern province of Quang Ninh have destroyed 111 illegal coal mines and arrested 15 pit owners in the past two months, a provincial official said on Tuesday.
The People's Committee official was confirming a newspaper report which also said that only 26 out of 200 illegal coal mines in the province were considered safe enough for workers.
Fatal accidents are not uncommon at coal and other mines in Vietnam, where rag-tag armies of migrant workers often toil in harsh conditions for very little pay.
"The situation is getting more serious because the dry season has started and farmers faced with a bad crop are flocking to Quang Ninh to look for a job," the official said.
"We must continue tough control on the situation. If we do not continue destroying these illegal private coal mines then the situation will become dire very quickly."
The government periodically launches blitzes on privately run coal mines, which it says are a threat to the environment and a competitive thorn in the side of the state-run Vietnam Coal Corporation.
Vietnam's coal production was 7.6 million tonnes in 1995, of which more than a third was exported.
